title: Son Lee Jr. becomes an entertainment attorney
summary: Lee steered his son toward entertainment law and got him jobs at Universal and then ABC as chief counsel and later Motown.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: At what point in your record company career did your son join you in the legal department? I know he's an attorney, right?
Yeah. Well, what happened -- my son was at the City Attorney's office, and I told him that I thought that he probably should go into entertainment law, you know.

I got him, probably pointed in that direction - we both attended USC and took a course in entertainment law one year, and it was kind of interesting to him, so that was just a way to give him a little feel of the thing.

And I heard that they needed an attorney out at Universal MCA, and I'd known a guy over there for years, and I called him and asked him, what about Lee, and he had known Lee since he was 6 or 7 years old -- and he was so surprised that he had turned out to be an attorney, so he said, 'Well, send him out.'

So I sent him out and he went out and they hired him. Well, he stayed there 2½ years, and then I was on a plane going to New York when I did the Broadway play, Two Gentlemen of Verona, and I recorded that in New York. And so I was commuting back and forth, and so I met the head counsel of ABC on the plane; we went back there together and he was from New York and he was saying that he was looking for an attorney to take over the west coast of ABC, and so I told him I just happened to have one for him.

And then he interviewed Lee and he hired Lee, and made Lee chief counsel and head of the legal department, and he had 4 other attorneys working under him. That was I think '71 ... no ... yeah, '71 it was when he came over.
So then he worked there until he came to Motown, and he came to Motown in October of '76, and don't be surprised
